verses.pali: Tatra kho āyasmā anuruddho bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: There Venerable Anuruddha addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato anuruddhassa paccassosuṁ.
“Cattārome, āvuso, satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā taṇhākkhayāya saṁvattanti.
verses.english: “Reverends, when these four kinds of mindfulness meditation are developed and cultivated they lead to the ending of craving.
It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ—
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: ime kho, āvuso, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā taṇhākkhayāya saṁvattantī”ti.
verses.english: When these four kinds of mindfulness meditation are developed and cultivated they lead to the ending of craving.”
